title: Autonomy
summary: Acting from your own deliberate choice, especially when pressure pushes you to react.

steps.heading: Autonomy
body: This topic looks at the difference between reacting to pressure and choosing how you respond.
Work through it one step at a time. Your place is kept on this device, so you can stop and come back.

steps.heading: What autonomy means here
body: Autonomy is acting from your own considered choice. It is not working alone, and it is not doing whatever you like.

Self-determination research treats autonomy as a basic psychological need, alongside competence and connection with others. When it is met, effort feels like your own. When it is squeezed, work can feel like a series of demands you are only answering.

steps.heading: The C³ Loop
steps.intro: Three moves you can repeat whenever pressure rises. Each pass makes the next one easier.

points.label: Centre
points.body: Settle your body first. A steadier nervous system makes clear thinking possible.

points.label: Clarify
points.body: Once steady, separate what is happening from the story you are telling about it.

points.label: Choose
points.body: Take one deliberate step that fits how you want to work, then return to Centre.

steps.heading: Reacting or choosing?
steps.instructions: Drag each moment into the group you think it belongs to. On a keyboard or phone, select a moment and then select a group.

items.text: Replying to an email the moment it arrives because it feels urgent
Checking what the email actually asks before replying
Agreeing to a deadline before looking at your week
Saying you will confirm the deadline by the end of the day
Taking one slow breath before answering a difficult question
Working through lunch because everyone else is

steps.feedback: There is no failing here. The aim is to notice the moment where a choice was available.

steps.heading: Your turn
steps.prompt: Think of a recent moment when you reacted rather than chose. What might Centre have looked like in that moment?
steps.placeholder: Write as much or as little as you like.

steps.body: A short recorded workshop working through the C³ Loop with a real example.

steps.heading: Take it with you

steps.heading: Bringing it together
points: Autonomy is acting from your own considered choice.
Centre, Clarify and Choose can be repeated whenever pressure rises.
Noticing the moment of choice is the first skill, and it improves with practice.
